items.name: Replacing One Model with Another
items.to:
When a rule tells you to place one model where another model was, or to replace one model with another:
▪ Mark the point on the battlefield beneath the centre of the base of the model to be replaced (or its central axis, for a unit with FRAME).
▪ Place the other model so that the centre of its base (or its central axis, for a unit with FRAME) is directly over that point.
If you cannot do the above because you would need to place one model on top of another model, or because you would need to place a model overhanging the battlefield edge, instead place the new model as close as possible to that point.

items.name: Drawing a Line
items.to:
When a rule tells you to draw a line, unless otherwise stated:
▪ That line has no thickness.
▪ That line must be straight.

fields.from:
Some rules may reference the term 'Desperate Escape test'. In all instances this means the **hazard rolls** made for the **desperate escape** mode of a **fall-back move**.
Abilities that subtract from a unit's Desperate Escape test instead subtract from those **hazard rolls**.
**Example:** A **battle-shocked** unit makes a **fall-back move** away from a unit of Bloodletters that have the Bane of Cowards ability. As a result of Bane of Cowards, because the unit making the **fall-back move** is **battle-shocked**, the **hazard rolls** they make as part of their **desperate escape** will be at -1.
fields.to:
Some rules may reference the term 'Desperate Escape test'. In all instances this means the **hazard rolls** made for the **desperate escape** mode of a **fall-back move**.
Abilities that subtract from a unit's Desperate Escape test instead subtract from those **hazard rolls**.
If a **stratagem** or ability instructs a unit to make a Desperate Escape test, that unit:
▪ Must use the **desperate escape** mode when it is selected to make a **fall-back move**.
▪ Must make one **hazard roll** for each model in that unit.
▪ Must make a **battle-shock roll**.
**Example 1:** A **battle-shocked** unit makes a **fall-back move** away from a unit of Bloodletters that have the Bane of Cowards ability. As a result of Bane of Cowards, because the unit making the **fall-back move** is **battle-shocked**, the **hazard rolls** they make as part of their **desperate escape** will be at -1.
**Example 2:** If an ability allows a unit to re-roll Desperate Escape tests, that unit can re-roll **hazard rolls** made for the **desperate escape** mode of a **fall-back move**.

fields.from:
At the start of the battle round, you can select one of the following Vows of Atonement to be active for your army until the start of the next battle round. You can only select each Vow of Atonement once per battle.
The Path of the Penitent
Add 3" to the Move characteristic of **PENITENT** models from your army.
Absolution in Battle
Each time a unit from your army is selected to fight, if that unit made a Charge move this turn, until the end of the phase, add 1 to the Attacks and Strength characteristics of melee weapons equipped by **PENITENT** models in that unit.
Death Before Disgrace
Each time a **PENITENT** model from your army is destroyed by a melee attack, if that model has not fought this phase, roll one D6. On a 2+, do not remove it from play; the destroyed model can fight after the attacking unit has finished making its attacks, and is then removed from play.

**ANATHEMA PSYKANA**
Though the Adeptus Custodes often fight alongside the Silent Sisterhood, they take orders only from their own commanders, or from the Emperor Himself.
You can include ANATHEMA PSYKANA units in your army, even though they do not have the ADEPTUS CUSTODES faction keyword.

▪ You cannot select ANATHEMA PSYKANA as your **army faction**.

Each time a unit from your army with this ability is selected to fight, select one of the Ka’tah Stances below. Until that unit has finished making its attacks, the selected Stance is active for it and it gains the relevant ability:
Dacatari Stance
Melee weapons equipped by models in this unit have the **[SUSTAINED HITS 1]** ability.
Rendax Stance
Melee weapons equipped by models in this unit have the **[LETHAL HITS]** ability.
fields.to:
At the start of your Command phase, friendly ADEPTUS CUSTODES units with this ability are **readied**. While a friendly unit is **readied**, you can select one of the **ka’tah abilities** presented below for that unit to use. If you do, that unit is no longer **readied**.
Each **ka’tah ability** will tell you when that **ka’tah ability** can be used, and the effects that **ka’tah ability** has on the unit using it.
We recommend placing a token next to each **readied** unit, removing it when that unit is no longer **readied**.
**Conversai**
**WHEN:** Your Command phase.
**TARGET:** One friendly **readied** unit.
**EFFECT:** Until the end of the turn:
Being **engaged/battle‑shocked** does not prevent your unit from being **eligible to start an action**.
Starting an **action** does not prevent your unit from being **eligible to shoot**.
**Calistus**
**WHEN:** Your Movement phase, when a friendly **readied** unit is **selected to move**.
**TARGET:** That **readied** unit.
**EFFECT:** When your unit makes a **normal/advance/fall‑back move**, your unit can move through all types of model.
**Salvus**
**WHEN:** Your Shooting phase, when a friendly **readied** unit is **selected to shoot**.
**TARGET:** That **readied** unit.
**EFFECT:** Your unit can ignore modifiers to your unit’s:
**BS.**
**Hit rolls** and **wound rolls**.
**Dacatarai**
**WHEN:** Start of the Fight phase.
**TARGET:** One friendly **readied** unit.
**EFFECT:** Your unit’s melee attacks that target an enemy unit (excluding MONSTER/VEHICLE units) can **re‑roll** hit rolls of 1.
**Kaptaris**
**WHEN:** Start of the Fight phase.
**TARGET:** One friendly **readied** unit.
**EFFECT:** Melee attacks that target your unit have -1 to **hit rolls**.
**Rendax**
**WHEN:** Fight phase, when a friendly **readied** unit is** selected to fight**.
**TARGET:** One friendly **readied** unit.
**EFFECT:** Your unit’s melee attacks have [LETHAL HITS: MONSTER/VEHICLE].
**Favoured Ka'tah**
Many of the most prominent shield hosts favour a specific martial ka’tah above all others.
All **detachments** tagged ‘Unique: Shield Host’ state a Favoured Ka’tah. If you selected one of these **detachments**, the **ka’tah ability** that is the Favoured Ka’tah of that **detachment** grants the additional effect listed in that **detachment**.
**Example:** If you selected the Solar Watch **detachment**, when you select the Calistus **ka’tah ability** for a **readied** unit, that unit has +2" **M** in addition to the normal effect of Calistus.

fields.from:
If your Army Faction is **ASURYANI**, at the start of the battle round, you receive a number of Battle Focus tokens based on the battle size, as shown in the table below.
Each time one of the triggers shown in the Agile Manoeuvres section below occurs, you can spend one Battle Focus token to enable the relevant eligible unit to perform that Agile Manoeuvre. A unit is eligible to perform an Agile Manoeuvre if it has this ability and has not already performed an Agile Manoeuvre in the same phase. Unless otherwise stated, you cannot trigger the same Agile Manoeuvre more than once per phase. At the end of the battle round, all unspent Battle Focus tokens are lost.
Agile Manoeuvres
When an eligible unit from your army is selected to make a Normal, Advance or Fall Back move. You can trigger this Agile Manoeuvre more than once per phase (provided a different unit performs it each time).
Until the end of the phase, add 2" to the Move characteristic of models in that unit.
When an eligible unit from your army is selected to make a Normal, Advance or Fall Back move, is set up on the battlefield, or declares a charge.
Until the end of the turn, enemy units cannot use the Fire Overwatch Stratagem to shoot at that unit.
When an eligible **VEHICLE** unit from your army is selected to make an Advance move.
Until the end of the turn, Ranged weapons equipped by this unit have the **[ASSAULT]** ability.
When an eligible unit from your army is selected to fight.
Until the end of the phase, each time a model in that unit makes a Pile‑in or Consolidation move, it can move up to 6" instead of up to 3".
When an enemy unit ends a Fall Back move.
One eligible unit from your army (excluding **TITANIC** units) that started the phase within Engagement Range of that enemy unit can make a Normal move of up to D6+1".
In your opponent’s Shooting phase, just after an enemy unit has shot.
One eligible unit from your army (excluding **TITANIC** units) that was hit by one or more of those attacks can make a Normal move of up to D6+1".
